findings.text: The reuse mask certifies a reused cell from its signed coefficients alone (`same_conic = jnp.all(signed == prior, axis=1)`) and never compares geometry.vertices, geometry.vertex_count, geometry.centre or geometry.pitch against the geometry the carried decision was built from, so a carried step whose mesh re-meshes while a cell's coefficients coincide returns the previous step's fragment areas and edge intervals; uniformly negative cells skip the interval comparison entirely (same_uniform clears only on exact edge-slot agreement when the cell is inside). Reuse is off by default so no production path reaches this today, but the opt-in the node exposes at topology.py:3638 is unsound for any caller whose geometry moves between steps.

`assert int(result[-1]) == int(jnp.sum(decision.normal_form_cells))` compares the recomputed count against the same represented population the function receives, so a mask that reuses nothing raises the count to exactly sum(normal_form_cells) and the assertion still holds; the regression the test name claims to catch (represented cells not refreshed) leaves it green, and only over-reuse reddens it. The unchanged-read test at line 39 closes the other direction for the fixture, so the durability score does not rest on this line.
